Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Kiwi openers, Will Young and Tom Blundell are out in the middle. Shaheen Afridi has the first new ball in hand.
... RUN CHASE ...

New Zealand too will be happy. They were disciplined with their bowling and got wickets at regular intervals. Just gave away a bit too many runs in the fag end but still this looks like a par total. Matt Henry was the best of the lot as he ended with three wickets. This is a decent pitch to bat on and if one of the Kiwi batters go onto play a big innings, they could win this one. Once again, the eyes will be on Tom Latham and Daryl Mitchell as Kiwis will hope a big innings from the experienced campaigners. Stay tuned for the chase.

Excellent finish from Shadab Khan and Pakistan will be happy with this score. They were too cautious with the start though. Zaman went cheaply this time but Imam-ul-Haq and Babar Azam combined to add over 100 and put Pakistan on the track for a big total. Azam fell after his yet another fifty. Imam-ul-Haq tried his best to stay till end and was all set for a big innings but unfortunately got out on 90. The good thing for Pakistan was the other batters made some kind of impact to get the total above 280.
SIX! Excellent from Khan! Fuller and outside off, Khan lofts it high and over long off for a biggie.  PAKISTAN END WITH 287.

TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and will BOWL first.

It is time for the third ODI between Pakistan and New Zealand. The home team have dominated the series so far as they are 2-0 up and a win here will do it for them. It is their batters who stepped up in both matches. For New Zealand, it is a must win game. They showed it in the T20I series after being 2-0 down and have to replicate the same effort to keep the series alive. From Rawalpindi, we travel to Karachi for the final phase of the series. Let's hope for an entertaining game. Stay tuned.
...Match Day...

Pakistan would be stepping up in the third ODI of the five-match ODI series with a 2-0 lead against the Kiwis, looking to seal the series with a win here at the National Stadium, Karachi. The hosts have been sensational so far in the ODI series as they have chased down the required totals with ease in both the games played so far. Babar Azam has had a quiet series so far but the ever-so-reliable Fakhar Zaman has stamped his authority till now being the Player of the Match in both games. Pakistan would be looking for contributions from others as well with the World Cup around the horizon. That key no. 4 spot for Pakistan is still up for grabs and the likes of Shan Masood and Abdullah Shafique should be looking to put in a more significant performance to stake a claim for it. New Zealand on the contrary would be taking on a lot of positives from the two games played so far. Despite the result not going in their favour. The Daryl Mitchell show on that no. 3 spot may have eased a few nerves preparing for the World Cup later this year in the absence of ace batter Kane Williamson. Chad Bowes has performed well too and the only area of concern in the batting unit is the scoring rate for them as they need to step up a bit more and accelerate the scoring rate in order to achieve more significant totals. The bowling unit has not impressed many, for the visitors, as they still search for that bowler whom the skipper can rely on in difficult situations. Many questions are yet to be answered for both sides with the series hanging by a thin thread for the Kiwis, we can expect a thriller.
